'''Nikita Alexandrovich Nekrasov''' ({{langx|ru|Ники́та Алекса́ндрович Некра́сов}}; born 10 April 1973)<ref name = "whoswho">{{cite book|title=Who's Who in France|year=2004|title-link=Who's Who in France}}</ref> is a Russian mathematical and theoretical physicist at the [[Simons Center for Geometry and Physics]] and [[C. N. Yang Institute for Theoretical Physics|C.N.Yang Institute for Theoretical Physics]] at [[Stony Brook University]] in [[New York (state)|New York]],<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.physics.sunysb.edu/Physics/people/people.php?group=faculty#NEKRASOVNIKIT |title = Stony Brook Physics & Astronomy: $group}}</ref> and a [[professor of the Russian Academy of Sciences]].

== Career ==
Nekrasov studied at the [[Moscow State School 57|Moscow State 57th School]] in 1986–1989.<ref name="CV">{{cite web|title=Nekrasov's CV at the IHES|url=https://www.ihes.fr/~nikita/CV2.html|access-date=6 September 2010}}</ref> He graduated with honors from the [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]] in 1995.  In parallel, in 1994–1996 Nekrasov did his graduate work at [[Princeton University]], under the supervision of [[David Gross]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=80896}}</ref> His [[Ph.D.]] thesis<ref name="Four Dimensional Holomorphic Theories">{{cite web|title=Nikita Nekrasov's PhD. thesis|url=http://media.scgp.stonybrook.edu/papers/prdiss96.pdf}}</ref> on ''Four Dimensional Holomorphic Theories'' was defended in 1996. There he introduced a four dimensional variant of [[Chern-Simons]] theory, rediscovered and developed by [[Kevin Costello]] in 2013. 
   
He joined [[Harvard Society of Fellows]] at [[Harvard University]] as a Junior Fellow 1996–1999.
He was then a Robert. H. Dicke Fellow at Princeton University from 1999 to 2000. In 2000-2013 he was a permanent professor at the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]]. Since 2013, he is a full professor at the [[Simons Center for Geometry and Physics]]<ref name="Nikita Nekrasov's CV">{{cite web|title=Nekrasov's CV at the SCGP|url=http://scgp.stonybrook.edu/people/faculty/bios/nikita-nekrasov|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref> and [[C. N. Yang Institute for Theoretical Physics]]<ref>{{cite web| title = People at the YITP|url=http://insti.physics.sunysb.edu/itp/www/people|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref>  at [[Stony Brook University]] in New York.

==Research==
Nekrasov is mostly known for his work on supersymmetric gauge theory, quantum integrability, and string theory. The [[Nekrasov partition function]], which he introduced in his 2002 paper,<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Seiberg-Witten prepotential from instanton calculus| journal=[[Advances in Theoretical and Mathematical Physics]] | volume=7| pages=831–864| arxiv=hep-th/0206161| last1= Nekrasov| first1=Nikita A.| year=2004|bibcode = 2002hep.th....6161N | doi=10.4310/ATMP.2003.v7.n5.a4 | s2cid=2285041 }}</ref> relates in an intricate way the [[instanton]]s in gauge theory, integrable systems, and representation theory of infinite-dimensional algebras.

== Honours and awards ==
{{BLP sources section|date=January 2021}}
For his discovery of noncommutative [[instantons]] together with [[Albert Schwarz]] in 1998,<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Instantons on noncommutative <math>\mathbf{R}^4</math> and <math>(2,0)</math> superconformal six-dimensional theory| journal=[[Commun. Math. Phys.]] | volume=198| pages=689–703| arxiv=hep-th/9802068| last1= Nekrasov| first1=Nikita|last2=Schwarz | first2=Albert| year=1998| doi=10.1007/s002200050490| s2cid=14125789 }}</ref> noncommutative [[Magnetic monopole|monopoles]] and monopole strings with [[David Gross]] in 2000 and for his work with [[Alexander Sergeevich Gorsky|Alexander S. Gorsky]] on the relations between gauge theories and many-body systems he was awarded the {{ill|Grand Prix Jacques Herbrand|fr}} of the [[French Academy of Sciences#Medals, awards and prizes|French Academy of Sciences]] in 2004. For his contributions to [[topological string theory]] and the [[ADHM construction]] he received the Hermann Weyl Prize in 2004. In 2008 together with [[Davesh Maulik]], [[Andrei Okounkov]] and [[Rahul Pandharipande]] he formulated a set of conjectures relating [[Gromov–Witten theory]] and [[Donaldson–Thomas theory]], for which the four authors were awarded the Compositio Prize in 2009<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://compositio.nl/prize|title = Compositio Prize}}</ref>.

Nekrasov was awarded the 2023 [[Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical Physics]] by the American Institute of Physics (AIP) and the American Physical Society (APS).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/heineman.cfm|title = Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical Physics}}</ref> for his “elegant application of powerful mathematical techniques to extract exact results for quantum field theories, as well as shedding light on integrable systems and non-commutative geometry.”

In 2024, [[Uppsala University]] of Sweden, awarded Nekrasov with an honorary doctorate.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Uppsala University, Sweden, Awards Prestigious Honorary Doctorate to Dr. Nikita Nekrasov – SCGP |url=https://scgp.stonybrook.edu/archives/43010 |access-date=2024-03-15 |website=scgp.stonybrook.edu}}</ref>
